finding.title: Fix docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's LWW tie-break rule — it contradicts the implemented and tested behavior
finding.rule: AG-8 (doc/code parity); FB-2/FB-3 (LWW ordering, clock-skew handling)

evidence.quote:
> strictly newer timestamp wins. If both timestamps are equal the remote row
> is silently dropped (the LWW rule is `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`).

// The one true tie (equal `updated_at`, no decisive server timestamp) is
    // resolved by preferring remote so two devices that wrote the same value
test('exactly identical timestamps, no synced_at → remote wins', () {

finding.why: The canonical doc says ties are dropped in favor of local (strict `remoteTimestamp > localTimestamp`) and never mentions a clock-skew window. The actual implementation and its exhaustive, intentional test coverage do the opposite for the common case: outside a ±5s skew window ties do stay local, but *inside* the window — the realistic case for near-simultaneous writes from a user's own two devices — an exact tie goes to REMOTE (code comment: 'prefer remote... converge instead of bouncing'), and a `synced_at` server-timestamp tie-break exists that the doc never describes at all. An engineer implementing a new merger or debugging a 'my edit got overwritten' report will read the doc, get the tie-break backwards for the realistic case, and either mis-implement a new merger or chase a phantom bug.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the 'Push/pull invariant' section to describe the actual 3-tier rule in DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer: (1) outside ±5s skew, strict remote>local wins and ties stay local; (2) inside ±5s skew with both sides carrying synced_at, the server timestamp decides; (3) inside the window with no decisive synced_at, remote wins to force convergence. Point the doc at drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 so future changes are easy to diff against it.
acceptance_criteria: docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md's tie-break wording matches lib/core/sync/merge/drift_merge_store.dart:113-152 exactly, confirmed by re-reading both side by side
the doc states the ±5s clock-skew window and the synced_at tie-break, matching DriftMergeStore.clockSkewTieBreakWindow

finding.why: All 24 files in this batch live under test/sync/, not the AG-5-mandated mirror of lib/core/sync/ (test/core/sync/), which already exists and is independently populated (12 files). For at least 9 of this batch's files the overlap is not just structural placement — it is the same merger/scenario tested twice: LearningLedgerMerger's snake_case-shape regression ('C1 regression' in learning_ledger_merger_test.dart) is retested by learning_ledger_roundtrip_test.dart's codec round-trip; StreakEventMerger's study_date-shape regression ('C2 regression') is retested by streak_events_roundtrip_test.dart; TrackConfigMerger/SettingsMerger/LearnerProfileMerger's LWW behavior (mergers_test.dart, against a hand-rolled fake MergeStore) is retested by curriculum_tracks_roundtrip_test.dart/learner_profile_roundtrip_test.dart/lww_symmetric_test.dart/persist_updated_at_test.dart (against the real DriftMergeStore); StageDefinitionMerger's schedule-shape and UiPreferencesMerger's 'no sacred_time clobber' behavior (codecs_and_mergers_test.dart, 1298 lines) is retested by stage_definitions_roundtrip_test.dart, location_device_scope_test.dart, and sacred_time_all_profiles_test.dart. docs/test-options.md documents test/sync/** as THE location for this coverage and never mentions test/core/sync/ existing — this is undocumented drift, not a deliberate two-tier split (both directories tag tests 'unit'). finding.recommendation: Pick test/core/sync/ as canonical (per AG-5's own 1:1 rule). For each duplicate pair, fold any scenario unique to the era-1 file (e.g. mergers_test.dart's fake-MergeStore isolation, if it adds value beyond the real-store versions) into the era-2 roundtrip test, then delete the superseded file. Update docs/test-options.md's test/sync/** references to match wherever coverage ends up.

finding.title: No test anywhere exercises FirestoreGatewayImpl's local-write-echo suppression (hasPendingWrites) — the 'listener echo of own writes' scenario this batch is charged with covering
finding.rule: FB-3 (skip LWW for hasPendingWrites/isFromCache); Nygard lens — mandated by this batch's AREA NOTE

evidence.quote:
// document's change carries `hasPendingWrites == true`. Re-processing that
    // self-write would loop the merge pipeline.

if (change.doc.metadata.hasPendingWrites) {
          localOnly.add(change.doc.id);
test('listenToCollection emits rows with firestore_id injected', () async {

finding.why: docs/test-options.md names test/sync/** as the home for this area's coverage, and this batch's AREA NOTE mandates the Nygard lens explicitly cover 'listener echo of own writes.' The production mechanism guarding against exactly that — filtering hasPendingWrites-only docChanges out of listenToCollection's emitted rows so a device doesn't reprocess its own optimistic write as an incoming remote change — has no test. Verified with `grep -rn hasPendingWrites test/` across the whole repository (zero hits) and by reading the listenToCollection test group in test/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart (the file that would naturally host it): none of its tests construct a pending-write snapshot or assert on this filter. The code's own comment names the failure mode being guarded against ('would loop the merge pipeline') — that mechanism can regress silently and nothing in CI would catch it.
finding.recommendation: Add a test (test/core/sync/firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart, or a new file under this batch's test/sync/ area) using fake_cloud_firestore's snapshot-metadata support, or a light hand-rolled fake at the docChanges/SnapshotMetadata seam, that: writes a doc, captures a snapshot where it appears only via a pending (not-yet-server-confirmed) local write, and asserts it is excluded from listenToCollection's emitted rows while a server-confirmed doc in the same snapshot is included.
acceptance_criteria: a new/updated test fails against a reverted firestore_gateway_impl.dart (one that emits regardless of hasPendingWrites) and passes against the current implementation

evidence.quote:
/// Mirrors `SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind`. Public copy used by the
/// supervisor's onEvent handler in this test. If the production switch
String? _channelToKind(String channel) => switch (channel) {
static String? _channelToKind(String channel) => switch (channel) {

finding.why: The test file's own comment admits the risk: 'If the production switch changes, this duplicate will diverge.' Because SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind is private, the test cannot call the real one, so it wires its own copy into the ListenerSupervisor under test and then verifies that copy against itself. If a future change re-routes a channel to a different EntityKind in production (not just adds a new channel) without a matching edit here, this suite keeps passing against its own stale copy while production sync silently misroutes — the exact failure mode the file exists to prevent. This isn't hypothetical: lib/core/sync/tutored_listener_supervisor.dart already carries an independent third copy of the same switch, textually different from both (it omits 'learner_profiles' and 'tutor_grants'), showing this table has already drifted once in this codebase.
finding.recommendation: Mark SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind @visibleForTesting (or extract it to a small shared top-level function, e.g. core/sync/sync_channel_kind.dart, imported by both sync_orchestrator.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart) and have new_listener_coverage_test.dart import and call the real function instead of maintaining its own switch.
acceptance_criteria: new_listener_coverage_test.dart no longer defines its own _channelToKind; it imports and calls the production mapping function

finding.title: Split test/sync/merge/lww_symmetric_test.dart (1237 lines) — 3x over the AG-3 400-line cap

evidence.quote: /// Phase 3 LWW symmetry tests for every LWW merger.

finding.why: 1237 hand-written lines — three times the 400-line ratchet the standard justifies as an 'agent read budget' — is why this file needed three separate Read calls during this audit. At this length the per-merger coverage is also uneven in a way that's hard to eyeball: some merger groups (BookmarkMerger, SettingsMerger, ProfileProgramMerger) get all 4 LWW invariants tested, others (LearnerProfileMerger, GoalMerger, NotificationSettingsMerger, GamificationSettingsMerger, UiPreferencesMerger) get only 2 — defensible here since the shared remoteIsNewer comparator is separately exhaustively unit-tested at the bottom of the same file, but that reasoning is only discoverable by reading the whole 1237 lines.
finding.recommendation: Split into one file per merger under a shared lww_symmetric/ directory, or convert to a single data-driven test iterating a List<MergerCase> table (merger instance + row builder + EntityKind + naturalKey) through the same assertions — shrinks the file and makes the per-merger coverage matrix explicit instead of implicit.
acceptance_criteria: the AG-3 checker (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) no longer lists lww_symmetric_test.dart
